title: Consolidation eliminations — Pine Holdings & Cedar Co.
instructions: Pine Holdings owns **100%** of Cedar Co. Prepare the Year 2 consolidation worksheet eliminating entries described below and compute selected consolidated balances. Ignore income taxes.

exhibits.title: Intercompany transactions
exhibits.content:
1. During Year 2 Pine sold merchandise to Cedar for **$150,000**; Pine's cost was **$100,000**. Cedar's December 31 inventory includes **40%** of these goods.
2. At December 31, Cedar owed Pine **$30,000** for these purchases.
3. On **January 1, Year 2**, Cedar sold equipment to Pine for **$84,000**. Cedar's carrying amount was **$60,000** (cost $100,000, accumulated depreciation $40,000). Pine depreciates it straight-line over **4 years**, no salvage. The gain is in Cedar's income; the equipment is in Pine's net equipment.

parts.prompt: Entry 1: eliminate the intercompany inventory sale and the unrealized profit in ending inventory (one combined entry).
parts.explanation: Eliminate the full internal sale (Dr Sales 150,000 / Cr COGS 150,000), then defer unrealized profit: (150,000 − 100,000) × 40% = 20,000 (Dr COGS 20,000 / Cr Inventory 20,000). Combined: Dr Sales 150,000; Cr COGS 130,000; Cr Inventory 20,000.

parts.prompt: Entry 2: eliminate the intercompany gain on the equipment sale and the Year 2 excess depreciation. Record the equipment adjustment net (the exhibit shows equipment net of depreciation).
parts.explanation: Gain = 84,000 − 60,000 = 24,000 — eliminate it. Pine's depreciation 84,000 ÷ 4 = 21,000 vs. group basis 60,000 ÷ 4 = 15,000 → excess 6,000 removed. Net equipment overstated by 24,000 − 6,000 = 18,000.

rows.label: Consolidated equipment (net)
rows.explanation: 700,000 + 410,000 − 18,000 = **1,092,000**. Check: group carrying amount of the transferred equipment = 60,000 − 15,000 = 45,000 vs. Pine's 84,000 − 21,000 = 63,000.
